𝗔𝗜 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟 𝗦𝗛𝗢𝗪𝗗𝗢𝗪𝗡: Meta Muse Ember vs. Spark vs. OpenAI Luna — What Can $META Earnings Tell Us About OTHER Stocks?

When Meta reports earnings, everyone focuses on META. But what about the suppliers, competitors, and other companies that could benefit or suffer from what management announces?

I tested Meta Muse Ember, Muse Spark, and OpenAI Luna on the same META earnings transcript, asking them to identify bullish and bearish implications for other stocks, including overlooked second-order effects.

All runs used high reasoning and web search.

𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗨𝗟𝗧𝗦:
• Muse Ember (T=0): 34 tickers in 33.5 seconds
• Muse Ember (T=1): 21 in 27.8 seconds
• Muse Spark (T=0): 15 in 130 seconds
• Muse Spark (T=1): 25 in 140 seconds
• OpenAI Luna: 19 in 395 seconds

𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗙𝗜𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚𝗦:

1. 𝗠𝗨𝗦𝗘 𝗘𝗠𝗕𝗘𝗥 𝗪𝗔𝗦 𝗜𝗡𝗦𝗔𝗡𝗘𝗟𝗬 𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗜𝗩𝗘.
34 potential winners and losers identified in just 33.5 seconds, versus almost 7 minutes for Luna!
The estimated token costs were also remarkably low, roughly $0.03–$0.09 per run, excluding web-search fees.

Ember's combination of speed, affordability, and discovery breadth really stood out.

𝟮. $𝗔𝗠𝗗 𝗪𝗔𝗦 𝗔 𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗣𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗜𝗡𝗚𝗟𝗬 𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗙𝗨𝗟 𝗧𝗘𝗦𝗧.

Given Meta's massive AI infrastructure spending, AMD seemed like an obvious potential beneficiary as an alternative GPU supplier to NVIDIA.

Yet only 3 of 5 runs identified AMD. Both Ember runs found it; both Spark runs missed it.

𝟯. $𝗕𝗞𝗡𝗚 𝗔𝗡𝗗 $𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗘 𝗪𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗨𝗟𝗔𝗥𝗟𝗬 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚.

I'd noticed these travel stocks sometimes appeared to move inversely to META around Muse-related AI news.

Ember identified the potential threat of AI agents disrupting traditional travel-booking platforms. Other models were more cautious or disagreed.

This is exactly the kind of indirect economic relationship I wanted to uncover, although the observed price movements don't establish causation.

𝟰. 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗦𝗢𝗠𝗘𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘𝗦 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗔𝗚𝗥𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗢𝗡 𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗔𝗠𝗘 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗔𝗡𝗬 𝗪𝗔𝗦 𝗕𝗨𝗟𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗛 𝗢𝗥 𝗕𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗦𝗛.

And more searching didn't necessarily mean more discoveries. Spark made up to 28 searches, while Ember found more companies with just 20.

𝗠𝗬 𝗧𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗔𝗪𝗔𝗬:

Muse Ember looks incredibly promising for AI-powered equity research and feels better than Spark even.

This is one experiment, not a definitive benchmark. More tickers don't necessarily mean better research.
